items: Work permit must be issued.

Use, only commercial g-d, new SF6 gas, moisture content
 will be less than15PPM and air content less than 0.05%

The filling of gas compartments should be done very slowly since
 the process will create a large temperature drop in the cylinder and supply
 hose.

For safe SF6 gas handling practice refer to Document No.
 TD-SS-005-r0
Clean the filling device (gas regulator and connecting hose)
Check that the Cylinder valve No. 1 and The valve No.2 are closed

Open the cylinder valve no. 1 for a very short moment to blow out the dust
 and close the valve again
Firmly connect the regulator to the cylinder valve

Open cylinder valve No. 1 and note the internal cylinder pressure on gauge
 (A) What should it be
 (260-320) Normal lower means 15 mpt 1

Turn the regulator adjustable gradually and adjust for the required
 filling pressure indicated on pressure gauge (B).
Connect the filling hose to the gas regulator

Open valve (No.3) on the regulator gradually to fill the hose with SF6
 gas, close valve (No.3) again

Attach the other end of the filling hose to the measuring point on the
 side of the valve cubicle

Again open valve No.3 on the regulator to fill the hose and all pipe
 connections up to the valves inside the valve cubicle

Now open the valve inside the valve cubicle corresponding to the gas
 compartment which requires filling

The corresponding pressure gauge will indicate which compartment requires
 additional SF6 gas if large amount of gas are added allow for temperature to
 stabilize

When the correct compartment pressure is reached, make certain that the
 valve inside the valve cubicle is tightly closed

If other compartments need topping-up in the same GIS breaker bay, repeat
 steps 11 to 13
Close valve No.1 on top of the SF6 gas cylinder

Disconnect the hose from the measuring point and screw on the
 flange cap
Close valve No. 3 and disconnect the hose from the regulator
Unscrew the regulator from the SF6 gas cylinder

Return the cylinder, the regulator and the filling hose to their proper
 storage space
Check any leakage of the gas from valve cubical or measuring point

text:
Substations | Technical Procedure
Introduction
Any SF6 gas filled switching equipment may experience a gradual loss of gas
pressure due to normal leakage. During routine inspections make sure that the gas
pressure is:
6.5 bars in conventional breakers 
 3AR1/EG or 8D4 breaker compartments in GIS equipment
3.2 bars in other bus compartments of GIS equipment.
In case the above pressures values are lower or a "loss of SF6 gas" alarm has
been indicated it is possible to refill (compensate) the leaked gas by simply
using a standard SF6 gas cylinder. There is no need to use the large gas
maintenance truck available in GIS stations. Use the following procedure below,
the diagram will help you to make the right connections
Safety Precautions
Work permit must be issued.
Use, only commercial g-d, new SF6 gas, moisture content
 will be less than15PPM and air content less than 0.05%
The filling of gas compartments should be done very slowly since
 the process will create a large temperature drop in the cylinder and supply
 hose.
For safe SF6 gas handling practice refer to Document No.
 TD-SS-005-r0
Work to be carried out
Clean the filling device (gas regulator and connecting hose)
Check that the Cylinder valve No. 1 and The valve No.2 are closed
Open the cylinder valve no. 1 for a very short moment to blow out the dust
 and close the valve again
Firmly connect the regulator to the cylinder valve
Open cylinder valve No. 1 and note the internal cylinder pressure on gauge
 (A) What should it be
 (260-320) Normal lower means 15 mpt 1
Turn the regulator adjustable gradually and adjust for the required
 filling pressure indicated on pressure gauge (B).
Connect the filling hose to the gas regulator
Open valve (No.3) on the regulator gradually to fill the hose with SF6
 gas, close valve (No.3) again
Attach the other end of the filling hose to the measuring point on the
 side of the valve cubicle
Again open valve No.3 on the regulator to fill the hose and all pipe
 connections up to the valves inside the valve cubicle
Now open the valve inside the valve cubicle corresponding to the gas
 compartment which requires filling
The corresponding pressure gauge will indicate which compartment requires
 additional SF6 gas if large amount of gas are added allow for temperature to
 stabilize
When the correct compartment pressure is reached, make certain that the
 valve inside the valve cubicle is tightly closed
If other compartments need topping-up in the same GIS breaker bay, repeat
 steps 11 to 13
Close valve No.1 on top of the SF6 gas cylinder
Disconnect the hose from the measuring point and screw on the
 flange cap
Close valve No. 3 and disconnect the hose from the regulator
Unscrew the regulator from the SF6 gas cylinder
Return the cylinder, the regulator and the filling hose to their proper
 storage space
Check any leakage of the gas from valve cubical or measuring point
